belief: Terrible things are about to happen to me.
origins: After loss, a bad diagnosis, trauma, or a pattern of anxious thinking, the mind keeps scanning for the next blow. Sleep and concentration suffer, and the future feels like a threat.
teaches: Jesus said, “Therefore do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Today has enough trouble of its own.” “Do not fear, for I am with you; do not be afraid, for I am your God. I will strengthen you; I will surely help you.” “Be anxious for nothing, but in everything, by prayer and petition, with thanksgiving, present your requests to God. And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus.” “Cast all your anxiety on Him, because He cares for you.” We cannot control the future, but we can trust the One who holds it.
self_statements: I am waiting for the other shoe to drop.
I will not be able to handle it.
errors: Feeling dread and concluding that danger is coming.
Focusing on threats and ignoring what is going well.
questions: How often have my worst predictions come true?
What has God brought me through before?
What is happening now that is okay?
What does Scripture say about worry?
What can I do today about this fear?
truth: I cannot predict the future, and most feared things never happen. God is with me and will help me with what comes, one day at a time. I can bring my fears to Him and receive His peace.
hw_truths: Today has enough trouble of its own.
He will strengthen and help me.
His peace will guard my heart.
log: Each week, note one fear that did not come true.
actions: Describe it and how likely it is.
Keep a log of fears and outcomes.
prayer: Lord, my mind runs ahead to disasters. Thank You that You are with me today. Give me Your peace, and help me trust You with tomorrow. Amen.
hw_questions: How often has it come true?
What has God brought me through?
name_example: Sarah can write: “I will not worry about tomorrow. God is with me today.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “Terrible things are about to happen to me.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
